description.summary: An ancient Greek analog computer from approximately 100 BCE, recovered from a shipwreck off Antikythera island in 1901. This complex geared mechanism was used for astronomical calculations and represents the most sophisticated mechanical device from the ancient world.
description.full: The Antikythera Mechanism is a remarkable artifact from ancient Greece, dating to approximately 100 BCE. Discovered in 1901 in a shipwreck off the coast of Antikythera island, it consists of at least 30 meshing bronze gears housed in a wooden frame. The device functioned as an analog computer to predict astronomical positions, eclipses, and calendrical cycles. While initially mysterious, extensive scientific study using X-ray tomography, surface scanning, and reconstruction has revealed its sophisticated engineering and purpose. The mechanism demonstrates advanced Hellenistic knowledge of astronomy and mechanical engineering, challenging earlier assumptions about ancient technological capabilities while fitting within the documented scientific achievements of the period.
